requirement:
Every `habeas author` form MUST accept `--missing` and `--force`, which are
mutually exclusive; `--missing` MUST be the default. Under `--missing`, the
command MUST assess only the selected subjects whose evidence is missing, stale,
or invalid, and MUST preserve every current record without invoking a model,
including accepted FIXME judgments and current false judgments; a current false
judgment is reassessed only when its subject or inputs change or `--force` is
given. Under `--force`, the command MUST assess every selected subject. `--stdout`
MUST imply `--force`, because it writes no evidence. The command MUST report the
number of selected subjects it skipped as current. When no assessment is needed,
the command MUST succeed without resolving model configuration or credentials.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each obligation in `requirements.authoring.refresh`. I did not request implementation source, because the supplied test text was enough to map every clause.

- **Flags accepted, `--missing` the default, mutual exclusion.**
  - `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[missing_keeps_current_records_and_force_reassesses_every_selected_subject]` runs a single requirement and `--all` with no flag and with explicit `--missing`. It also runs `--force`.
  - The same test asserts that `--missing` with `--force` fails with "cannot be used with", for both a single subject and `--all`.
  - The same test asserts that `--stdout` with `--missing` fails, because `--stdout` already implies `--force`.
  - `fn[site_reviews_are_authored_by_requirement_and_orphans_deleted_by_all]` and `fn[batch_authors_citation_reviews_and_preserves_current_ones]` run the site and citation forms with the default, `--missing`, and `--force`.
  - The `author-evidence` form is exercised under the default.
  - I found no mutual-exclusion test for the site and citation forms. The text states mutual exclusion once for every form, and the tests cover it for the single-subject and `--all` forms.

- **Assess only missing, stale, or invalid subjects.**
  - `fn[a_single_missing_or_stale_subject_is_assessed_under_default_or_explicit_missing]` assesses a missing record. It then edits the subject text so the record is stale, and checks that both the default and `--missing` reassess it and that the next run skips it.
  - `fn[batch_fills_evidence_preserves_current_records_and_reauthors_only_changed_inputs]` changes a read input and asserts exactly one subject is reauthored. A change to an unread item causes no model call.
  - `fn[batch_reauthors_a_false_judgment_when_its_reference_set_changes]` covers a changed reference set.
  - `fn[missing_keeps_current_records_and_force_reassesses_every_selected_subject]` writes `{invalid` into a record and asserts `--missing` reassesses it.

- **Preserve current records, including accepted FIXME and current false judgments.**
  - The first batch test hand-edits `requirements.beta` to a FIXME determination. After the later runs it asserts that record, the example records, and the gamma records are unchanged.
  - `fn[batch_preserves_current_false_judgments_and_reauthors_stale_ones]` marks records false. It checks that the current false records stay byte-identical and are not reassessed, that a stale false record (gamma, after its test changed) is reauthored, and that `--force` reassesses alpha.
  - `fn[default_authoring_apis_preserve_current_records_without_configuration]` checks byte-for-byte preservation through `author_all`, `author_evidence`, and `author_evidence_with_output`. It also checks that no usage record is started.

- **`--force` assesses every selected subject.**
  - `--all --force` yields "6 authored; 0 skipped as current".
  - Forced runs of a single requirement, a site review, and a citation review each call the model again and overwrite a tampered record, using a sentinel rationale.
  - `fn[policy_comes_from_the_flag_then_the_configuration_then_defaults_to_confirm]` also runs with `--force` and asserts "0 skipped as current".

- **`--stdout` implies `--force`.** `fn[missing_keeps_current_records_and_force_reassesses_every_selected_subject]` asserts a model call for a current subject under `--stdout`. The citation test covers `--stdout` on a citation form.

- **Skipped-as-current count reported.** Summaries such as "0 authored; 6 skipped as current; 0 failed" and "1 authored; 5 skipped as current; ..." are asserted for mixed and all-current runs. Single-subject runs assert "evidence is current; 1 skipped as current (use --force to reassess)".

- **No configuration or credentials when nothing needs assessment.** Current-record runs succeed with invalid TOML (`not toml [`) and with the config file removed. This is shown for single requirement, example, `--all`, site, and citation forms. The unit test uses an unconfigured backend selection that would fail if it were resolved.

No unacknowledged gaps remain.
